title: Georestriction policy composer and automated attestation pipeline for hosted endpoints
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Several enterprise customers require per-tenant enforcement of geographic constraints for Hosted API requests (data residency) plus an auditable artifact proving where customer data was processed and retained. Current hosted endpoints are routed by region affinity but lack a customer-facing composer for granular georestriction rules, nor an automated evidence export that packages attestable proofs (route traces, retention snapshots, and signed metadata).

Problem statement: We need a product and implementation plan to: (1) expose a safe, simple UI and management API for customers to declare georestriction policies (allow/deny regions, soft affinity, hard lock, fallback policy), (2) persist and enforce those rules in the routing layer with deterministic fallbacks, (3) capture and package region+retention evidence per request/commit into a tamper-evident export for audits.

Goals: Provide a composer UX and management API for tenant georestriction; implement server-side enforcement and deterministic fallbacks; add retention controls per-tenant/region; emit an automated attestation bundle (signed manifest + traces + retention proofs) that customers or auditors can fetch on demand. Meet enterprise compliance expectations (ISO/ SOC-like evidence), maintain < 1% increase in P95 latency for pinned tenants, and avoid cross-region residual storage.

Scope: This ticket covers product design, management API schema, routing enforcement contract, evidence bundle format (spec), telemetry requirements, and rollout plan for Hosted API. Implementation tasks are split into ENG epics. Out of scope: on-prem packaging and Dedicated capacity UI changes (handled separately).

Non-functional constraints: Must integrate with existing KMS for signing evidence bundles; evidence storage must be immutable and access-controlled; rollouts must be reversible with canary for 5% of pinned traffic before full enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: PM UX: Composer allows tenant admins to create policies with allowlist/denylist, fallback tier selection, and retention overrides; changes saved and versioned.
API: Management API accepts policy objects and returns a policy id; validation rejects contradictory rules and surfaces human-friendly errors.
Runtime: Routing service enforces hard locks and returns a deterministic routing decision; soft-affinity honors latency/cost policy with explicit fallback reason codes.

Evidence: For each policy change and for periodic snapshots, the system can produce an attestation bundle (signed manifest + request trace excerpts + retention snapshots) accessible via management API.
Telemetry: Console shows per-tenant residency compliance events, pin conflicts, enforcement rate, and evidence export status.
Security: Evidence bundles are signed with KMS key and audit log contains who requested/consumed bundles.
Performance: End-to-end median latency for pinned endpoints remains within target; canary rollout demonstrates <1% error/latency regression.
Docs: Public docs and admin-facing help text for composer and evidence export published before GA.
Legal: Compliance team signoff on evidence format and retention semantics recorded in PRD.
Rollout: Canary at 5% for 72 hours, verify metrics, then gradual ramp to 100% with rollback plan documented.
updates: 2025-02-20: Scoping workshop with Compliance, Runtime, Console. Agreed hard vs soft policy semantics and required evidence elements.
2025-02-24: Spike (ENG-6249) landed — routing decision API extended to emit 'residency_reason' codes; prototype traced path for canary requests.
2025-02-27: UX review — simplified composer iteration accepted; removed freeform rules to reduce ambiguity and audit surface.
2025-03-04: Engineering spike complete; KMS signing integration pattern validated against existing archived-exports flow. Draft PRD updated with evidence manifest schema.
Next: Scheduling cross-team RFC for evidence storage retention and export S3 layout; target signoff 2025-03-10.
qa_plan: QA will run policy unit tests (validation, edge cases), e2e canary traffic with synthetic tenants in multiple regions, evidence bundle integrity checks (signature verification), and regression tests for non-pinned tenants. Include chaos tests for region outage to validate fallback behavior.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged internal canary for 5% of tenant traffic (48h smoke + 24h monitoring), 2) Opt-in customers: invite 10 customers for early access, 3) Gradual ramp to GA over 2 weeks with health gates (latency, errors, evidence export success). Rollback: revert feature flag and invalidate in-flight evidence exports; publish incident report if rollback triggered.
notes: Trade-offs considered: Allowing highly expressive rule DSL increases audit complexity — we constrain composer to declarative allow/deny + tiered fallback to simplify proofs. Retention overrides are per-tenant-per-region and are stored as immutable policy versions. Evidence bundle format chosen is zipped JSONL traces + signed manifest for interoperability with customer auditors.
